how: Members call ents into canvas work, from generic invitations to requests to secure a particular coordinate.
Members ask what the canvas is and how to reach or use it, while replies explain access, placement rules and the work's history.
Explaining the giant canvas receives an explicit intention to visit after getting home, supporting one explanation-to-participation link rather than universal recruitment.
Short replies volunteer help or report a contribution without asking anything back.
A placement request receives the bare commitment I gotchu in a direct reply, supporting the written acceptance pattern rather than claims about silent readers.
A call to establish a shared presence receives a direct report of a pixel contributed to the proposed leaf.
Participants judge the available labour insufficient for restoring the pineapple and propose a smaller mark.
A host-room member threatens departure over canvas-related drama, without establishing that an identified active builder abandons placement.

statement: Touring the canvas without reporting a commitment to build
how: Members invite touring or describe looking at the canvas without reporting a placement commitment in those turns.
A member proposes a mark or reports construction begun, independently of whether anyone later joins.
A post reports pineapple construction already begun at a coordinate and immediately calls others to help that specified work.
Participants choose leaves, pineapples, lettering, colours and a symbolic coordinate while revising what represents the room.
Contributors report pixels placed, work progressing and previously visible work disappearing.
Members share coordinates and pixel templates and ask for a common form to follow.
Posting a template settles design only for informed participants, since helpers unaware of the revision keep restoring the previous version.
Invitations move helpers into Discord, and participants bring designs and treaty reports back without exposing the chat's deliberation.
Helpers missing a redesign does not establish intentional concealment from rivals, spying or coded strategy.
Members describe a pattern-setting script and additional accounts as ways of working on the intended mark.
Repeated repair and tool use are visible without a demonstrated transition from exhausted manual capacity to adopting automation.
Members schedule participation around getting home, work and a seminar, and later recall hours spent placing and relief after closure.
Participants report an apparent extra-pixel opportunity and a successor site failing to load, without verifying persistence of extra pixels or the proposed overload diagnosis.
Descriptions of unorganised work coexist with local teams and explicit repair priorities, preventing an inference that all decided order is absent.

statement: Making member art into a working subreddit header
how: Members nominate independent art, a moderator installs it, and contributors repair its dimensions and styling during live canvas activity.
A member-art exchange becomes a recruitment opportunity when replies redirect creative effort toward the canvas without demonstrating transfer of the artwork.
Members defend and harden the mark while unknowingly repairing away a planned redesign until its explanation reaches them.
An announcement that the room appears on the canvas receives a call to save its dissolving drawing.
Participants discover their own mistakes and uninformed redesign resistance behind some changes previously read as hostile interference.
Bringing the backstage redesign into public view elicits recognition, apology and reallocation of repair effort from helpers who had obstructed their own side.
Members choose initial coordinates, edit a proposed location and accept a sideways adjustment to avoid changing more pixels without naming a loss as the reason.
Neighbours condition coexistence on nonoverlap, propose combined designs, report truces and remind participants of their agreements.
Members apologise for encroachment, ask others to stop expanding and refuse to vandalise neighbouring team efforts.
A neighbour arrives with a compromise proposal while a local participant reports approaching another room for a truce.
A participant explicitly explains seeking a truce by the useless expenditure of pixels on the other room.
A neighbour's repeated border complaint receives acknowledgements that the ribbon is intrusive and expansion should stop while maintenance continues.
The smaller mark is incorporated into a neighbour's template and frame through a proposed compromise and references to approval.
Neighbouring projects request maintenance, exchange placement promises, report completion and thank helpers.
A neighbouring room's flag-maintenance appeal receives a completion report and thanks, showing outside help from the receiving side rather than proving every request succeeds.
A truce and subsequent assistance are reported without evidence that border negotiation caused the assistance.
Invitations to band together and join a defensive alliance do not establish completed coalition accession or reciprocal coalition defence.
An alliance offer addresses contested territory, but neither its acceptance nor coalition defence against a common threat is demonstrated.
Participants propose relocation or a smaller restoration after losses without establishing a completed collective move.
Too few contributors can prompt reducing the design at the existing symbolic coordinate rather than abandoning defence of that place.
A participant describes Quebecois, stoner and Canadian belonging as an internal conflict, and the reply says these identities fit the plan together.
Disorganisation, a treaty violation accusation and an invitation for project leaders do not explicitly state limits on who may commit the room.
Reported negotiations and uninformed interference do not establish a post-agreement statement that others cannot be bound or a refusal of the agreement.
Cannabis symbols, the numbered coordinate and familiar forms of address provide recognisable marks and affinities for calls and help.
The revenge proposal names a canvas invasion rather than establishing a quarrel carried from before the canvas.
Cannabis identity and legalisation references accompany alteration calls without establishing an earlier rivalry as the reason for targeting that neighbour.
The final lettering defect generates treeg renaming, pizels jokes, proposed flair and suggestions for a new subreddit.
Acceptance that placement has ended and the lettering cannot be fixed directly occasions proposing a new subreddit without demonstrating its creation.
A canvas-specific Discord is reported started and another post describes a server gathering logo builders, without establishing a new subreddit or identical servers.
The mock defence of personified pizels does not resolve whether calling a joke harsh constitutes an offence objection or continues the joke.
Fake quitting and legalisation claims are revealed or challenged as April Fools performances alongside genuine replies and routine moderation.
Members object to repeated canvas calls and request containment while moderators defend a coordinating sticky and enforce ordinary posting rules.
Explicit complaints about recruitment spam motivate containment requests while a moderator explains the sticky as help for existing builders.
Complaints about canvas posts do not report retaliatory sabotage of the room's own mark, and friendly mistakes do not establish that intent.

statement: Carrying ordinary conversation alongside event work
how: Event threads carry political self-defence and bot banter, while prank threads develop genuine health advice outside their organising or joking functions.
Members celebrate a recognisable surviving mark while acknowledging its broken final letter and imperfect pixels.
A display of the coordinate's current state receives direct congratulations for the group's organisation.
Participants circulate timelapses and screenshots, recount destruction and rebuilding, claim contributions and describe the ending.
Celebration and recording intermingle, including a timelapse before final-image posts, without establishing that celebration caused preservation.
Finding a better screenshot and joking about treeg or tree9 do not establish cleanup requests or correction of a historical claim about the work.
Participants invite renewed work on successor canvases, with access problems and limited responses rather than demonstrated collective migration.
A successor builder explicitly recreates the previous pineapple at its old coordinate, carrying the remembered plan rather than a demonstrated saved image.
Seeing the mark prompts a visit to check whether it belongs to the room, without establishing first discovery, new membership or subscriber growth.
A legalisation slogan and thanks from a canvas neighbour do not establish directing the work toward represented creators, staff or press outside the canvas.
Members call for altering neighbours' leaves, numbers and figures, sometimes explicitly seeking a quick laugh.
Recruitment to alter figures and later contribution reports do not trace previously recruited builders turning their labour against rivals.
Members argue against covering neighbouring work by calling it vandalism of a team effort and questioning damage while their own mark needs upkeep.
Attack proposals receive direct refusals grounded in respecting collective work or prioritising defence of the room's own mark.
A suggestion to alter a neighbour's figure receives a treaty reminder, while another receives advice to seek that neighbour's agreement first.
Participants answer an attack accusation with territorial entitlement and later blame accounts allegedly created to vandalise their work.
A neighbour's attack accusation receives a territorial counterclaim, supporting a minimal reported-attack-to-contest-talk exchange without independently verifying who altered the pixels.
